title: Information formatting in neuronal populations predicts differential functional contributions to behavior
title_zh: 神经元群体中的信息编码预测行为贡献的差异性功能作用
abstract: Neurons throughout the brain encode essentially everything, so why have distinct areas? We proposed that areas format different information sources differently, implying their computational role. Here we compared the middle temporal (MT) area, involved in visual motion perception, and the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC), implicated in decision-making and reward. In a task that required monkeys to combine motion and reward information, both regions encoded both motion and reward, but formatted differently. Area MT represented them separably, whereas the dlPFC combined them in a decision-related format. A recurrent network model trained to reproduce that formatting predicted a distinct effect of stimulating those areas. Consistent with predictions, MT stimulation biased choices whereas dlPFC stimulation produced ‘winner-take-all’ outcomes. Our findings suggest that a modular structure flexibly reformats information to enable complex behaviors. Using experiments in monkeys and modeling, the authors demonstrate that the formatting of population information predicts the contribution of different brain areas to behavior.
abstract_zh: 大脑中的神经元编码了基本上所有内容，那为什么会有不同的区域？我们提出，不同区域以不同方式编码信息源，这意味着它们的计算角色。在此，我们比较了参与视觉运动感知的中旁回（MT）区域和参与决策和奖励的背外侧前额叶皮层（dlPFC）。在要求猴子结合运动和奖励信息的任务中，两个区域都编码了运动和奖励，但编码方式不同。MT区域将它们分别编码，而dlPFC则以决策相关的格式将它们结合。一个经再现训练的循环网络模型预测了刺激这些区域的不同效应。正如预测的那样，MT区域的刺激偏向选择，而dlPFC刺激产生‘胜者全有’的结果。我们的发现表明，模块化结构可以灵活重新编码信息以支持复杂行为。利用猴子实验和建模，作者展示了人口信息的编码预测了不同脑区对行为的贡献。
